title: Build checkout delivery and payment selection UI
verify: Only the existing authenticated_ready gate renders the FT-006 form; UI state never substitutes for backend actor authorization.
The form collects name, email, phone, city, conditional address, optional comment, one of the three backend-provided delivery methods, and one of card/sbp/sberpay.
Delivery methods render in stable order and show backend-resolved tariffs rather than client constants.
Field validation, conditional address, delivery_method_unavailable, retry, alternative selection, and sanitized unexpected failure states are rendered deterministically.
The client sends normalized contract input through the backend boundary and does not call an order or payment provider directly.
A successful response is represented as validated FT-007/FT-009 handoff, not order/payment success.

verify.reason: Direct dependency TASK-047 is blocked by upstream TASK-046 and cannot provide the backend contract required for this UI task.
verify.operator_action: Resolve TASK-046, then execute TASK-047 before promoting TASK-048.

verify.reason: Direct dependencies TASK-047 and TASK-032 are done; TASK-047 backend contract and independent T3 gates are closed.
verify.operator_basis: Scheduler promotion after TASK-047 closure and strict-doctor deadlock diagnosis.

verify.reason: T2 implementation, required packet/spec gates, full protocol, and independent functional verification passed.

evidence_required: Storefront state matrix and field/conditional-address test output.
Synthetic UI evidence for stable options/tariffs, unavailable recovery, and payment IDs.
Storefront typecheck and Memory Bank lint output.
constraints: Reuse the FT-004 checkout auth gate and do not redesign authentication or cart merge.
Use backend option/tariff truth; do not duplicate or hardcode the tariff table in the client.
Keep payment selection to card, sbp, and sberpay without provider integration.
Do not create orders, inventory reservations, payment attempts, or browser-authoritative checkout records.
Keep UI errors sanitized and avoid rendering customer PII from backend failures.
invariants: Only authenticated_ready may render checkout continuation.
Pickup does not require address; courier and transport-company do.
Unavailable delivery requires retry or explicit alternative selection.
Local UI success cannot bypass backend validation or imply order/payment success.
purpose: Provide the buyer-facing authenticated checkout continuation for the FT-006 contract.
success_outcome: An authenticated buyer can enter valid checkout data, see current configured delivery tariffs, select a payment ID, recover from unavailable delivery, and receive a validated handoff state without provider/order behavior.
anti_goals: Do not implement OAuth, cart merge, order creation, inventory, or payment-provider integration.
Do not store authoritative checkout data or tariff values in browser storage.
Do not mark a local form submit as order/payment success.

stop_conditions: The backend contract cannot provide current option/tariff data and stable errors.
The existing authenticated_ready gate cannot isolate checkout continuation.
UI behavior requires direct order/payment-provider calls or browser authority.
Unavailable recovery would silently replace the selected method.
